title: Pope meets Villanova and Notre Dame basketball teams at the Vatican
summary: The teams are in Rome for the U.S. college basketball season opener — an event dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off and created to honor the U.S.-born pope.
story: Pope Leo XIV met on Saturday with the basketball teams from Villanova and Notre Dame, along with thousands of U.S. fans in Italy, ahead of the two Catholic universities' season opener later this weekend.
About 7,000 people entered the Paul VI audience hall inside the Vatican on Saturday after a special private Mass in St. Peter's Basilica.
Leo, who is an avid tennis player and sports fan, said sports bring people together and can promote values such as fraternity, solidarity and peace.

"By acting as a concrete means of bringing people together, athletics can teach the values of cooperation and mutual sharing.  This is increasingly necessary in an age marked by the distance that can be created by technology," he said, according to Vatican News.

The teams are in Rome for the U.S. college basketball season opener on Sunday — an event dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off and created to honor the U.S.-born pope. The universities' men's and women's teams will play a doubleheader at the Palazzo Dello Sport, an 11,000-seat arena about a half-hour drive from the Vatican.
Leo, who is currently recovering from lung cancer surgery, graduated from Villanova in 1977 with a Bachelor of Science in mathematics.

"Growing up on the south side of Chicago, we oftentimes heard, 'Go Irish.' But as you all know, Prevost graduated from Villanova! So, the Pope doesn't take sides. Prevost has another opinion, but we won't do that now," Leo joked during the audience, according to Vatican News.
Leo urged the teams and their families to embrace sports as a way to grow in saintliness.
"No one is born a champion, just as no one is born a saint," he said.
He warned against letting sporting rivalries get out of hand and he said he hoped the fans in Rome this weekend would actually get to know one another as they cheer, "even passionately."

"In any competition, the members of two teams, even when they have a competitive rivalry, are certainly not enemies," he said. "I hope, therefore, that despite the competitive nature of college basketball, there will be opportunities for the players and the fans of both teams to get to know each other in your days here in Rome."

Before the audience, the Rev. Robert Dowd, president of Notre Dame, acknowledged Villanova had something of an edge considering it counts the pope as an alumnus. But in an interview Saturday, he said the occasion to bring both teams together with all their fans in Rome for a papal audience and season opener was "amazing."

"That could be a little challenging, but I know that the pope is a pope for all of us, and so I'm grateful," he said. "I know in a particular way the pope talks about the importance of bridge building, and I'm sure he'll be a bridge builder when we play each other."

Philadelphia Archbishop Nelson Perez celebrated a private Mass for traveling fans in St. Peter's Basilica on Saturday morning, and asked the thousands of people in the pews to give a round of applause to the players. The English-language liturgy was unusual in that it had all the trappings of a papal Mass celebrated at the main altar and televised live by Vatican Media.

Asked about the upcoming games on the papal plane during a recent trip to France, Leo said, "They tell me that the people coming to the match, 90% are Villanova and 10% Notre Dame, so the voice of the people of God will be very strong on the Villanova side."
Leo is an avid Chicago White Sox fan and has been known to follow basketball, too.

"He will know who they (the players) are. He's a true, blue Villanovan," said the Rev. Rob Hagan, Villanova's longtime team chaplain. He said Leo used to attend Villanova games at the Palestra, the Philadelphia arena known as "The Cathedral of College Basketball."
Sunday's games coincide with All Saints' Day, a major Catholic holiday.
"Our true goal, beyond emerging victorious in any one event, is to win the prize of everlasting life," Leo said.

title: U.S. approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged his allies to speed up deliveries of the critical munition.
story: The State Department approved on Friday the sale of 500 Patriot missile defense systems to Ukraine at a cost $2.1 billion.

In a statement released Friday, the State Department said the purchase will be paid for by Ukraine with donations from Canada and European allies such as Germany and Norway, and that no U.S. funds are involved in the sale.

"This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe," the department said. It also added the principal contractor in this agreement is Lockheed Martin and that there would be "no adverse impact" on U.S. defense readiness.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy lauded the decision, and thanked President Trump, but warned that it may take years for the munitions to be delivered to Ukraine.
"We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger," Zelenskyy appealed on Friday evening.

In a post on X, the Ukrainian president said there had been more than 30 Russian strikes on his country's energy infrastructure in the past two weeks, targeting "the systems that sustain life in our cities and communities."

He appealed to the United States and European allies to provide Ukraine with the Patriot systems currently in their own stockpiles and replenish their arsenals with these 500 missiles, purchased by Ukraine, in the coming years.
"We are asking for decisions that can guarantee the protection of lives not the day after tomorrow or sometime later, but at the very moment the threat is there," Zelenskyy added.
Ukraine has long warned of dwindling supplies of Patriots, which it uses to intercept strikes from Russia, and has previously accused the U.S. of slowing down deliveries of the critical missiles.
The development comes amid ongoing tensions between Ukraine's president and Mr. Trump, who faced criticism for waiving new sanctions on Russia just days before they were expected to take effect.

title: How hard is it to recover the $6 billion stolen from Binance?
summary: Security experts are calling it the "largest bank robbery in human history." Getting all of the stolen crypto funds won't be easy.
story: After hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance, the cryptocurrency exchange said Friday it is working to recover the assets, a multi-pronged process that experts said involves coordinating with law enforcement and tracking the movement of the stolen funds.

"Binance has begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds," a Binance spokesperson said in a statement to CBS News.

Ari Redbord, a former federal prosecutor and the global head of policy at TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence company tracking the stolen funds, called the heist the "largest bank robbery in human history."

TRM and other security firms attributed the attack to an elite hacking unit linked with North Korea known as "TraderTraitor." The funds were siphoned from internet-connected wallets on Binance's trading platform, Redbord said. The entire operation took roughly 20 minutes, according to Binance.

"The way a cryptocurrency exchange works is basically just like a bank. People put their funds in the bank, and those funds go onto wallets that are controlled by the exchange," Redbord told CBS News. "What North Korea was able to do was breach the hot wallets where Binance was keeping all of those funds."
As it works to recover the stolen assets, Binance vowed in a social media post to cover the full losses using company funds.
"We will pursue all available avenues to identify those responsible and hold them accountable," Binance said.
How does the recovery process work?
Redbord called the effort to recover Binance customers' funds the "fastest and largest" he's ever seen.

The first step involved blocking the hackers from transferring the funds. Within an hour after the attack, stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether had frozen $2.4 billion of the stolen assets, he said. Ripple and World Liberty Financial, the Trump family's crypto venture, also froze assets, according to TRM Labs.

Issuers of stablecoins — a type of cryptocurrency pegged to a stable asset, such as the U.S. dollar — can block transfer of their tokens anywhere in the world, speeding the recovery effort. A total of $3 billion in crypto assets have been frozen, the Binance spokesperson told CBS News.
However, roughly $2.4 billion in stolen funds consist of bitcoin and ether — those funds are now "beyond any issuer's reach," according to a blog post from TRM Labs.
Bitcoin and ether "move on public blockchains, and they cannot be frozen," Redbord said. "That is a very, very specific capability that [only certain] stablecoin issuers have."
The best shot at recovering those funds is if the thieves try to convert the crypto to regular currencies, including cash, he added.
In a social media post, Binance said that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, while a subsequent probe uncovered additional "points of breach."
The cyberattackers are now likely laundering the stolen funds to evade detection by law enforcement, according to Redbord.
How long could it take to recoup the funds?
To actually recover the frozen funds, stablecoin issuers will start by moving the assets into a wallet that North Korea cannot access, he said.

"Law enforcement will follow up with what they call a 'seizure warrant,' which basically says we need you to actually physically transfer these funds to a U.S. government account," Redbord told CBS News.
After the funds are seized, government officials will have to pursue a civil forfeiture proceeding in court to recover the crypto assets.

"The government must show that the funds were associated with the activity at issue," Redbord said. "It is the final step before the funds can be taken permanently from the bad actor and given to the government or victims."

Any of the Binance funds that aren't recovered could be used by North Korea to carry out illicit transactions with countries like Russia, Roman Bieda, chief intelligence officer at Recoveris, a Swiss blockchain intelligence company, told CBS News.

"Freezing assets and recovering them are two very different things," he said. "North Korea has a history of using stolen cryptocurrency to circumvent international sanctions and finance its activities."
In 2025, TraderTraitor also targeted another crypto exchange, Bybit, in an attack resulting in a $1.5 billion loss, according to the FBI.

Given the scale of the Binance theft, it's unclear how long it could take for the crypto exchange to recoup the stolen assets. In one case, Bieda said his team worked for a Swiss client in which it took 14 months to recover $10.5 million in stolen crypto.

"The process remains unpredictable," he said in an email, emphasizing the close coordination required between law enforcement, crypto issuers and other stakeholders to track down the funds. Figuring out where the money went is only half the battle, he said.
"Knowing whom to contact and reaching them before the assets move again can make all the difference, and this is really challenging," Bieda said.

title: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in a U.S. election
summary: The Vatican said Pope Leo exercised his right as a U.S. citizen, submitting a mail-in ballot in his native Chicago ahead of the midterm elections next week.
story: Pope Leo XIV has become the first pontiff to vote in a U.S. election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the American-born pope submitted a mail-in ballot in his native Chicago ahead of November's midterm elections, citing his longstanding belief in civic participation.
The pope, formerly Cardinal Robert Prevost, "has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so," the Holy See press office said.
"The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes," the Vatican said in a statement.
The Will County Clerk's Office confirmed to CBS News that he is on the list of voters who requested a mail-in ballot, with a registered address in New Lenox.

The Chicago Sun-Times first reported Leo's vote and quoted the chief of staff at the Will County Clerk's Office as saying the pope requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. This was just days before his recent lung cancer surgery.
The pope has been recovering and resuming his activities at the Vatican after being released from the hospital Oct. 17 and is moving ahead with plans for a trip to South America next month.
Last month, Leo told a general audience at the Vatican that the faithful should leave behind "all passivity and indifference" toward current events.

"We cannot remain as unengaged spectators; rather, we must listen with our hearts, allow ourselves to be challenged, and become involved," the pope said on Sept. 2 in St. Peter's Square, according to the Catholic News Service. "With Christ and sustained by the power of his Spirit, believers are called to take on the burdens of their brothers and sisters, especially those who are crushed by injustice, discrimination and violence."

The pope has a long history of civic engagement in the U.S., the Vatican said, confirming that during his nearly two decades as a missionary then bishop in Peru, Leo voted whenever he was eligible. He holds U.S. and Peruvian citizenship.

According to records from the Illinois State Board of Elections, the pope, as Robert Prevost, was registered to vote in Cook County. The Associated Press reports he previously voted in five primary elections since 2000 — on the Democratic ballots in 2008 and 2019 and Republican ballots in 2012, 2014 and 2016.
Illinois has closed primaries, which means voters must declare a party preference to receive a ballot. No such declaration is required in general elections.
The pope submitted ballots in every general election since 2000, except in 2020 and 2022, the AP reported, citing Illinois election records.

title: Ukrainians trapped in Russia-held city evacuate during local ceasefire
summary: Russian strikes on the surrounding area have prevented food, water, and medicine from reaching the city for months.
story: Kyiv - Ukrainian and Russian humanitarian delegations began evacuating residents from Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday, with plans to move the evacuees through Russia and Belarus before arriving back in Ukraine on Saturday.

Oleshky, a city in Ukraine's southeastern Kherson region occupied by Russia since the first days of the Ukraine-Russia war, has seen one of the most dire humanitarian crises of the conflict. Russian strikes on the surrounding area have prevented food, water, and medicine from reaching the city for months. Last week, first lady Melania Trump brokered a temporary ceasefire in Oleshky from Oct. 28 to Nov. 1 to allow humanitarian aid to enter, and for some residents to evacuate the area. Pope Leo also pressed for a truce.
On Friday morning, Ukrainian and Russian humanitarian delegations reached the city and began administering aid and preparing for evacuations.

"Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to leave safely. At the same time, those who have decided to stay can stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian support," Ukraine's Human Rights Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, who led the Ukrainian delegation, said.
The convoy included 25 buses, and some ambulances arrived to deliver food and medicine. Local authorities say about 2,000 people remain in Oleshky.

The localized ceasefire comes after President Trump increased pressure on Kyiv to stop striking Russian energy targets ahead of the U.S. midterm elections next week, with some Ukrainian officials doubting Russian motives.

"Because these negotiations were led by the U.S. and Melania Trump, it seems to me that the Russians have agreed to this ceasefire to show that they are a reliable partner for these negotiations and other future peace negotiations with Ukraine," Vadym Ivchenko, a Ukrainian parliament member on its Defense, Intelligence, and National Security Committee, told CBS News.
But on social media platforms, Ukrainians expressed skepticism about the local ceasefire, and what it could mean for Ukraine's broader Kherson region, in the midst of its own humanitarian crisis.

"Under the pretext of evacuating people from Oleshky, they are moving their troops forward. This poses a direct threat to the city of Kherson and the Right Bank," Ukrainian journalist Nastia Nagorna wrote on Facebook. "This risk escalates if such humanitarian missions become a 'monthly' occurrence—or take on any other form of 'regularity.' It would allow Russian forces, under the guise of delivering humanitarian aid, to amass a significant concentration of troops and resources."

Fighting has continued elsewhere during the localized ceasefire. On Thursday afternoon, a Russian strike on a passenger train station in Ukraine's eastern city of Dnipro killed at least 14 people. Overnight into Friday, Russia launched an attack on Kyiv's energy grid, leaving hundreds of thousands without power, while Kyiv struck a Russian oil refinery for the first time in two weeks.

title: Internal documents show failed scramble to save "forever cruise"
summary: The MV Odyssey was billed as a continuous around-the-world cruise when it launched in October 2024. It ended abruptly in Cambodia.
story: When the journey of the MV Odyssey luxury cruise ship came to a sudden end earlier this week in Cambodia, giving residents on the ship just hours to disembark, it marked the culmination of several attempts over a period of about three months to save the unique voyage.

According to accounts from multiple sources familiar with the final weeks on board, those included a scramble to find fuel while stuck at a port in Singapore, a rush by the crew to obtain provisions once food shipments had ended, and the temporary detainment of the ship in Hong Kong.

The voyage of the Odyssey, which is operated by Florida-based Villa Vie Residences, was billed as a continuous around-the-world cruise when it launched in October 2024. It allowed passengers to become residents of the ship by purchasing cabins for several hundred thousand dollars.
However, more than 200 passengers and dozens of crew members became stranded in Cambodia on Tuesday when Villa Vie suddenly suspended operations because of major financial issues.
In early August, the Odyssey was docked in Singapore when Villa Vie warned that the ship was at risk of being detained and the operator said it urgently needed to raise money.
"There's no question that we ran out of money in Singapore," said Darrell Carp, a Villa Vie resident who told CBS News he is out $250,000.
Residents believed finances were being mismanaged by cruise operator
Multiple residents told CBS News they were concerned about giving money directly to the company because they believed the finances were being mismanaged by Villa Vie.
"We never fully understood the level of their debt," Carp said. "They were already behind on their payments on crew, and provisions, and fuel, and things like that."
A source close to the company said that when fuel prices spiked this year after the U.S. attacked Iran, it was a disaster for the company's business model.

After some passengers raised money while the ship was stuck in Singapore, $400,000 was paid to a fuel supplier directly out of one resident's personal checking account so the Odyssey could continue its journey, sources said.

At that time, Villa Vie was in the hole for several million dollars, according to internal documents reviewed by CBS News. Hundreds of thousands of dollars were owed to a port agent, fueling companies, food vendors and the crew.
Those internal documents showed that in a town hall on Aug. 4, residents were warned there was a real possibility of halting operations, laying off staff and repatriating the crew.

According to documents reviewed by CBS News, the ship was potentially days away from losing its insurance. It said that it would cut internet service to save money and was paying just enough to keep sailing.
Villa Vie introduced VIP program to raise emergency funds

In early August, Villa Vie introduced a so-called VIP "Villa Incentive Program" to help raise emergency funds, according to the documents. The VIP program was only open to current Villa Vie passengers so they could purchase more cabins at a discounted rate.
By Aug. 18, the company posted: "We have the commitment of over 20 cabins on the VIP sales!"

The program was initially an idea by the residents. Instead of just raising funds, it was designed to give passengers an even greater ownership stake in the ship, according to passengers and a source close to the company.
There was urgency to sell the cabins. The last slide of a PowerPoint presentation by Villa Vie on the VIP program read, "Funds are due today."
The VIP program was able to raise enough funds to keep the ship operating, but it continued to struggle, sources said.
A source with knowledge of the VIP program also said cabins aboard the Odyssey were still being sold to Villa Vie residents despite the company operating at a loss at that point.

According to one document, the ship's finances showed that even at full occupancy, it would operate at a $600,000 loss. Average monthly operating costs were $3.1 million, but revenue at 100% occupancy with everyone paying full fees would only have been $2.5 million, the document showed.
A source close to the company disputes the $3.1 million number and claims that the ship's monthly operating costs were under $1 million.
In August, 139 of 490 cabins were unsold, according to the documents.
Ship director had to bribe Vietnam officials to get food aboard, source says

When the ship reached Vietnam, crew members allegedly had to buy food from local grocery stores to feed passengers because the company owed money to a food vendor that would no longer deliver food, according to sources familiar with the situation.
According to one source, the ship's hotel director allegedly had to bribe local customs officials in Vietnam in order to get food onto the ship.
Later, in Hong Kong, court records obtained by CBS News showed the ship was detained until the company paid $167,844.48 to a fuel provider.
Villa Vie founder Mike Petterson has said skyrocketing fuel costs were what ultimately caused the ship's journey to come to an end.

When asked by CBS News Wednesday if creditors might seize the ship, Petterson told CBS News: "We will likely file for Chapter 11 here any day, right, which will put a stay on that while we go through the restructure process."
A source close to the company said Villa Vie stopped conducting cabin sales externally after Aug. 4, once the ship knew it was essentially out of money and needed to raise funds.

Yet on July 27, just a week before the ship ran out of money, Villa Vie had announced it was in the process of purchasing a second ship, the Legacy, and offered residents who were buying a cabin on the future ship an opportunity to take up immediate residency on the Odyssey.
A source close to the company said it was necessary to buy more ships to scale up for the business model to work.

title: Brittany Aldean says husband Jason is 'always there' with advice as she builds venture of her own
summary: Brittany Aldean reveals her grandmother Louvada inspired VADA, her fragrance brand, and shares how Jason Aldean supports her entrepreneurial journey.
story: Brittany Aldean shares how her grandmother inspired her new fragrance line, VADA, and opens up about the challenges of building a beauty business more than a decade in the making.
Brittany Aldean has been busy building a business of her own.

After spending more than a decade considering a venture in the beauty or fashion industry, the wife of country superstar Jason Aldean launched VADA, a fragrance brand inspired by someone close to her heart.
"My inspiration behind VADA itself, the name and everything was my grandmother," she told Fox News Digital.
"Louvada was her name, so I used a beautiful abbreviation for the name. And she was just all things beauty. And I feel like that's where I got everything from."
Brittany Aldean recently opened up to Fox News Digital about launching her fragrance brand, VADA, and balancing business with family life. (Getty Images for SabesWings.org)
BRITTANY ALDEAN WOWS IN VACATION STYLE DURING BAHAMAS GETAWAY WITH JASON ALDEAN

BRITTANY ALDEAN REVEALS FAMILY INSPIRATION BEHIND NEW FRAGRANCE BRAND VADA
"And so, after about over a decade of thinking about it, I landed on personal fragrance," she said.
Turning that idea into a business, however, proved more demanding than she anticipated.

"I think the personal investment in launching a business is massive," Brittany said. "I didn't really realize, and now it's really just the time frame of everything and how long things take if you really are passionate about something and a perfectionist like I am."
She spent more than two and a half years developing the brand before bringing her products to market.

Brittany admitted that entering the fragrance industry was initially intimidating, particularly as she learned the technical side of developing scents.
"We've visited the labs where they make all the scents and everything, and I just feel like it's been such a learning experience," she said.
BRITTANY ALDEAN GETS CANDID ABOUT BALANCING MARRIAGE, MOTHERHOOD AND BUSINESS
The personal connection to her grandmother extends beyond the company's name.
Brittany revealed that her signature best-selling fragrance, 1924, was named after the year Louvada was born.
Jason has also played a supportive role in Brittany's entrepreneurial journey.
Brittany revealed that she had turned to her husband for business advice earlier that same day while he was back home in Nashville caring for their children.

title: Ricki Lake says Rosie O'Donnell was 'judgy' about her facelift then got one herself after weight loss

title: Heidi Klum leads celebs with over-the-top couples' Halloween costumes through the years
summary: Over the years, Heidi Klum's green Medusa prosthetics stole the show, but Selena Gomez, Paris Hilton and Kourtney Kardashian also delivered iconic couples looks.
story: ‘America’s Got Talent’ judge Heidi Klum tells Fox News Digital she doesn’t want to give away too much when it comes to this year’s Halloween costume.
Couples' costumes on Halloween are always fan favorites, and even more so when it's a celebrity couple.

Heidi Klum and her husband look unrecognizable on the red carpet every year in head-to-toe prosthetics, while Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr. have referenced iconic movies from the '80s in the past.
Here are some of the best couples' Halloween costumes from over the years.
Klum and Kaulitz leave fans waiting every year for their Halloween couples costume reveal. (Getty Images)
Heidi Klum and Tom Kaulitz
Klum and Kaulitz dressed up as Medusa and someone she turned into stone at her Halloween party in 2025. (Taylor Hill/WireImage)
The official Queen of Halloween always goes above and beyond for her annual Halloween party, and her husband, Tom Kaulitz, plays along each year.

At her party in 2025, the couple looked unrecognizable as they posed for photos on the red carpet. Klum dressed as the Greek mythological character, Medusa, while Kaulitz dressed as a warrior she had turned into stone.

Heidi Klum and Tom Kaulitz attend Heidi Klum’s 24th Annual Halloween Party presented by Butterfinger and Huluween on Disney+ at the Hard Rock Hotel New York on Oct. 31, 2025. (Noam Galai/Getty Images for Heidi Klum Halloween)
The costume consisted of a full green prosthetic bodysuit with scales and a tail following behind her, with fake teeth and a crown of snakes on top of her head, which actually moved.

"I love for people to see this and think whatever they want to think for the first time when I go on the red carpet," she told Fox News Digital in 2024. "I never like to share it before, because then people are gonna be like, ‘Oh, it wasn’t as good as I thought it was gonna be.'"
Kaulitz and Klum turned heads as different versions of E.T. in 2024. (Noam Galai/Getty Images for Heidi Klum Halloween)
In 2024, Klum and Kaulitz arrived to the annual Halloween party dressed as different versions of E.T. from the hit '80s movie, "E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial."

Kaulitz dressed as the more traditional version of E.T., while Klum dressed as the version of the character from when the kids in the movie try to disguise him, donning a black hat, blonde wig and red shawl.
Klum dressed as the version of E.T. that was in disguise. (Sunset Boulevard/Corbis via Getty Images)

"As a 9-year-old in Germany, E.T. introduced me to the idea that there’s life outside planet earth," she said on Instagram. "I know E.T. wanted to go home, but I hope that if the movie took place in 2024, that my favorite extra terrestrial would come to my party instead."
Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco
Gomez and Blanco embraced their madness when they dressed as Alice in Wonderland and the Mad Hatter in 2024. (Selena Gomez Instagram)
Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco were late for a very important date as they followed the white rabbit down the rabbit hole and into Wonderland for Halloween in 2024.

The couple dressed as Alice in Wonderland and the Mad Hatter, with Gomez wearing a whimsical blue dress with white socks and a blonde wig. Blanco wore black pants with a brown jacket and multicolored undershirt, paired with a big top hat and an orange wig, as he got into character with white face makeup.
"Curiouser and curiouser.." Gomez captioned the Instagram post.
Paris Hilton and Carter Reum
Paris Hilton and Carter Reum dressed up as Britney Spears from the "Toxic" music video and an airline pilot. (Michael Kovac/Getty Images for Casamigos)
Paris Hilton channeled her inner Britney Spears when she dressed as the singer in her music video for "Toxic."

The 45-year-old media personality posed for photos at the Casamigos Halloween Party in 2023 in a futuristic blue flight attendant uniform, which she paired with metallic silver-heeled boots and sunglasses.
Reum was all smiles as he stood next to her donning an airline pilot uniform.
Kourtney Kardashian and Travis Barker
Kardashian and Barker dressed up as Beetlejuice and Lydia on their wedding day for Halloween in 2023. (Kourtney Kardashian Instagram)
"I’m the ghost with the most, babe," Kourtney Kardashian captioned a 2023 Instagram post featuring her and Travis Barker in their ghoulish Halloween costumes.

The celebrity couple dressed up as Beetlejuice and Lydia Deetz at their wedding. Barker wore white makeup on his face with dark circles around his eyes, paired with green hair and a burgundy red suit, perfectly capturing the essence of the spirit.

Kardashian embodied his blushing bride in a red dress with a lace neckline and sleeves, and wore her hair in an intricate updo as she posed for the photo with a serious expression and holding a bouquet of roses.
Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber
Gerber and Crawford dressed as different pop icons from the 80s in 2018. (Michael Kovac/Getty Images for Casamigos)
Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber embraced their inner rock stars when they dressed as David Bowie and Debbie Harry at their Halloween party in 2018.

Gerber's costume consisted of black pants and a black shirt, which he paired with a Union Jack flag coat, a red and white scarf tied around his neck and a spiky orange mullet wig. He also painted a red lightning bolt over one of his eyes to emulate Bowie's alter ego, Ziggy Stardust.

Crawford, on the other hand, wore a yellow T-shirt dress over ripped-up black tights and knee-high heeled boots with a black belt around her waist and a red handbag. She styled her hair in a big blonde wig and wore heavy eye makeup.
Lisa Rinna and Harry Hamlin
Rinna and Hamlin channeled one of television's favorite couples, Lucy and Ricky Ricardo. (Steve Granitz/WireImage)
One of reality TV's most iconic characters dressed up as one of TV's most legendary icons, when Lisa Rinna and her husband Harry Hamlin cosplayed Lucy and Ricky Ricardo from "I Love Lucy."

title: Tatum O'Neal steps out with family ahead of 63rd birthday years after near-fatal stroke
summary: Tatum O'Neal's outing with family follows years of recovery from a stroke, seizures and cardiac arrest after an overdose during the COVID-19 pandemic.
story: The actress was spotted walking with a cane in Los Angeles in an all-black outfit with her daughter and son-in-law.
Tatum O'Neal was recently spotted enjoying a day out with her family in Los Angeles.

The "Little Darlings" star was photographed at a fan convention with her family wearing a black dress paired with a coat, glasses and layered necklaces. She styled her hair in an updo and walked outside the convention with the assistance of a cane.
O'Neal was accompanied by daughter Emily McEnroe and son-in-law Tim Massarelli.
The sighting comes ahead of the actress' 63rd birthday Nov. 5 and more than six years after she had a near-fatal stroke in May 2020 after an overdose on morphine, opiates and pain medication.
O'Neal was photographed in an all-black outfit during the recent outing.  (Backgrid)
'LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE' STAR SAYS CHILD ACTORS GET 'DROPPED' AFTER HOLLYWOOD FAME FADES

In a July 2023 interview with People, O'Neal and her son, Kevin McEnroe, opened up about the health scare, with her son telling the outlet there were moments when he and his siblings, Sean and Emily, "didn't think she was going to survive."
McEnroe shared that, in addition to the stroke, O'Neal had multiple seizures and went into cardiac arrest. She spent six weeks in a coma.
O'Neal was spotted out in Los Angeles with her daughter and son-in-law. She is pictured here in 2018. (Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for New York Magazine)

O'Neal has struggled with drug addiction for decades, and McEnroe said she "had become very isolated" during the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic and had begun abusing medications, including some prescribed to her to treat neck and back pain and rheumatoid arthritis.

"She had become very isolated," he told People. "With the addition of morphine and heavier pharmaceuticals, it was getting scary. COVID, chronic pain, all these things led to a place of isolation. In that place, I don't think, for her, there was much hope."

O'Neal had a near-fatal stroke in May 2020 that left her in a coma for six weeks. (Paul Archuleta/FilmMagic)
O'Neal made her feature film debut in the 1973 movie "Paper Moon," which she starred in alongside her famous father, Ryan O'Neal, at 9 years old.

She went on to make history for her role in the film as the youngest winner of a competitive Academy Award when she took home the award for best supporting actress at the 46th Academy Awards in 1974, when she was 10 years old.
"All I really want to thank is my director Peter Bogdanovich and my father. Thank you," she said in her acceptance speech.

While she thanked her father in her speech, the two had a turbulent relationship. In her 2004 autobiography, "A Paper Life," Tatum shared that their relationship first became rocky after making "Paper Moon" because he was jealous of her success.

title: 'Baywatch' star Nicole Eggert exposes financial toll of cancer battle: 'The bills don't stop'
summary: Nicole Eggert revealed the financial toll of her breast cancer battle as a single parent, from lost income to mounting bills during treatment.
story: Actress Nicole Eggert explained the real cost of her cancer diagnosis to Fox News Digital.
Nicole Eggert admitted that finances are a neglected conversation when it comes to fighting cancer.
Eggert, 54, was diagnosed with Stage 2 cribriform carcinoma breast cancer in December 2023. Two years later, the actress revealed her cancer status was "NED," or no evidence of disease.

While the "Baywatch" star is a survivor of a club she "never wanted to be a part of," Eggert told Fox News Digital the financial strains of her battle added an entirely different stressor to her life.
BRANDI GLANVILLE SPEAKS OUT ON COMPLEX DIAGNOSIS AND $6K MONTHLY MEDICAL BATTLE
"Baywatch" actress Nicole Eggert shared the financial realities of battling breast cancer. (Olivia Wong)

"I'm a 100% single parent," Eggert explained. "One of my daughters is an adult, so she is very self-independent, and she does great, but I do have a teenager still at home. ... I have that responsibility, and then I have all the household and homemaker, head of household responsibilities and then the cost of what this diagnosis brings, which is a lot. … Really, you can't even wrap your head around it."
‘BAYWATCH’ STAR NICOLE EGGERT SAYS IT'S ‘VERY HARD TO BE HEALTHY IN AMERICA’ AS SHE BATTLES CANCER
Eggert noted that the costs consistently "add up," so much so that she was afraid of being able to provide for her family.

"In my line of work, I couldn't commit to being on any kind of production because I'm gonna be in treatment and in and out of treatment ... three to five, at least, days a week," she said. "So, it's not like it's work from home kind of work.
Nicole Eggert has one teenage daughter, Keegan, and an adult daughter named Dilyn. (Amanda Edwards)

"I had to completely come to the realization that I wasn't gonna have income, and yet the bills don't stop. And the teenagers still need their things. And life needs their things and the car still needs the gas. And, you know, all of it."
The "Charles in Charge" actress noted that when she took a step back and looked at the disease, "money seemed very trivial."
LINDA PERRY SAYS SHE WAS FEELING HEALTHY WHEN DOCTORS DISCOVERED ‘ANGRY’ CANCER BY CHANCE

"It's sort of like, well, 'Ah, I'm alive.' Then, you know, if you have any kind of financial strain, it's like, 'Well, at least you're alive to deal with it,'" she said. "At least you are alive where you can go out and fix it.
"I had to completely come to the realization that I wasn't gonna have income."
"So, there's that part too, where suddenly you're like, 'Wow, whatever. It's just, it's just money.' And that comes and goes. So, you know, it's ebb and flow of life."
Nicole Eggert was shocked to realize the financial strains of cancer. (Getty Images)
In December 2023, after experiencing unexplained weight gain and pain in her left breast, Eggert was diagnosed with a rare form of breast cancer.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

She underwent her first mastectomy soon after and later explained that she'd wanted to do a double mastectomy at the time, but her doctor advised that if she just had one breast removed, she'd be able to get into treatment faster, and her immune system wouldn't take as big a hit. So, she agreed.
WATCH: 'Baywatch' star Nicole Eggert details financial toll of cancer battle
Over a year later, in August 2025, she had her other breast removed, and surgeons performed a reconstruction.
Eggert admitted that one major component in her cancer journey was being able to rely on her community.
Nicole Eggert, best known for her role in "Baywatch," shared that she underwent a hysterectomy after troubling test results. (Getty Images; Nicole Eggert/Instagram)

"You really have to find your community, and you really have to be OK with asking for help or asking other people how they do it and getting tips and tricks and just all the information you can get," she said.
"That's why these conversations are just so, so important and so necessary. Because what else would you do?"
As part of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Eggert partnered with Novartis and shared a little more insight into her cancer journey on the "Voices of More" podcast with Amy Robach and Dr. Helen Coons.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Eggert explained how helpful it can be for women to get together, share stories and find interwoven commonality in experiences.

"If we keep talking about these things, it becomes so much easier to talk about, and maybe we don't feel like we have to hide things anymore because in the past it's not ... it's kind of been a taboo topic," she said.
"And now I think more and more women are becoming more comfortable to discuss what their journey looks like, what it feels like, how it's gone for them."
Nicole Eggert noted that while her oldest daughter was independent, her teenaged daughter still relied on her financially. (Robin L Marshall/Getty Images)
While the past has its place, Eggert is looking forward to the future and spending more time enjoying life to the fullest with her family.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I also am really looking forward to stepping back into life not having to be in treatment or in the treatment facility with this newfound power and fearlessness that I have and this new appreciation for life that I have, and It's like this second chance at life," she said.
"I know that that's so cliche, but it's to jump back in with all of these crazy changes that have happened in the past two years, three years. There's been very, very big changes inside myself.

"So, to be able to now go back into life and get back into the workforce and get back into doing things I enjoy with this new mindset, it's exciting. It's exciting."

title: Tim McGraw says brutal toll of filming 'Yellowstone' prequel pushed him to edge: 'Wouldn't have survived'
summary: Between 14-hour days and late-night flights for concerts, Tim McGraw says filming Taylor Sheridan's "1883" was the hardest job he and Faith Hill ever had.
story: Eric Nelsen and LaMonica Garrett share what it was like bringing the Western drama to life. The series, created by Taylor Sheridan, originally became available for streaming in December 2021. The show is now airing on Paramount Network.
Tim McGraw was pushed to the brink while filming Taylor Sheridan's Western drama "1883."
The country music superstar revealed that the brutal production schedule left him questioning how much longer he could keep going.

Between 14-hour shooting days, six-day workweeks and late-night flights for concert performances, McGraw said the grueling experience was unlike anything he and his wife, Faith Hill, had faced before.
"If it had gone on any longer, I probably wouldn't have survived, put it that way," McGraw told Esquire.
MATTHEW MCCONAUGHEY GIVES UPDATE ON RUMORED 'YELLOWSTONE' SPIN-OFF SERIES, YEARS AFTER REPORTS FIRST SURFACED
Tim McGraw said the grueling filming schedule for Taylor Sheridan's "1883" pushed him to his limits with 14-hour days and six-day workweeks taking a brutal toll. (Terry Wyatt/WireImage)
The "Live Like You Were Dying" singer described the demands of filming the "Yellowstone" prequel.

"I learned a lot, certainly because it was such a tough shoot," McGraw said. "I think we shot for right around six months. It was a long shoot. Five or six months. It was close to it. And we shot mostly six days a week, and like 14 hours a day."
But filming wasn't McGraw's only commitment.
The country star was also juggling concerts, sometimes going straight from the set to an airplane before returning home in the middle of the night and starting the cycle again just hours later.

Country superstar Tim McGraw recalled juggling exhausting days on the set of "1883" with concert performances, sometimes getting just hours of sleep between commitments. (Christopher Polk/Billboard via Getty Images)

"And during that time, I had a handful of shows that I had to do," he explained. "So, there were times that I would finish up around six o'clock in the evening, jump on a plane, go do a show and then get home at one in the morning, then be in the gym at three and be in the makeup chair at 5:30, six. So, I had a few of those."

Although "1883" followed the Duttons' journey from Texas to Montana, much of the series was filmed in Texas before production moved north. The cast also endured a rigorous cowboy camp, learning to ride, rope, work cattle and shoot guns before filming began.

"We all got to do it together, which was an incredible experience," "1883" co-star Eric Nelsen previously told Fox News Digital. "But it was a time for us to get comfortable on our horses, to learn how to cut cattle, how to rope, how to shoot guns — all the things we're going to have to do on the show."

The real test came on set. McGraw and Hill recalled filming a dangerous river crossing around 3 a.m. on their 25th wedding anniversary, with temperatures hovering around 36 or 37 degrees, according to Entertainment Weekly.
The grueling schedule left little room for sleep or recovery.
"I told Faith it was probably the hardest job we've ever had. I had some hard jobs growing up."
McGraw then revealed how close the demanding schedule had pushed him to his limit.
Tim McGraw and Faith Hill portrayed James and Margaret Dutton in Taylor Sheridan's Western drama "1883," which follows the family's dangerous journey across the Great Plains. (Rich Fury/Getty Images)
Despite the physical demands, McGraw said the experience was worth it, particularly because he got to work alongside Hill and Sheridan.
MICHELLE PFEIFFER FOUGHT 'BATTLE' WITH TAYLOR SHERIDAN BEFORE SURRENDERING TO HIT SHOW 'THE MADISON'
"It was tough, but it was worth it because we were getting to work together, and we were getting to work with Taylor, who was fantastic, and, like I said, a brilliant writer."
McGraw also said he gained a greater appreciation for preparation, explaining that the demanding production taught him the importance of arriving on set ready to work.
Although McGraw had previously appeared in films, "1883" marked his first major role in a television series. The demanding shoot also required McGraw to contend with unpredictable conditions on set.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"The elements were always fighting us, and you were working with animals, and you were working with extras, and you were working with horses, which I grew up riding horses, so it was fun for me," McGraw said.

"But I think I learned more than anything is there's so much value in preparing. And the more you prepare and the more you're ready to do what you're going to do, it takes away a lot of the nervousness."

Tim McGraw described filming "1883" as one of the toughest jobs he and Faith Hill had ever faced but praised Taylor Sheridan's writing and said the demanding experience was worth it. (Omar Vega/Getty Images)
McGraw and Hill starred as James and Margaret Dutton in "1883," which follows the couple's perilous journey across the Great Plains in search of a new life in Montana.

title: Former Miss USA contestant made a life-changing decision at 26 after cancer devastated family
summary: Allyn Rose lost nearly every woman in her family to breast cancer before choosing a preventive double mastectomy that even sparked hate mail.
story: After losing her mother and several relatives to breast cancer, former Miss USA contestant Allyn Rose made a life-changing decision to break her family's cancer legacy.
At age 26, Allyn Rose made a life-changing decision after cancer had devastated her family.
The model, who competed in both the Miss America and Miss USA pageants, underwent a preventive double mastectomy, a decision she said even sparked "hate mail" from critics.

Today, the mother of two is the founder of The Previvor, a nonprofit organization that educates women about breast cancer risk and prevention options. Oct. 31 marks the last day of Breast Cancer Awareness Month.
KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’
"I know a lot of people think that's a pretty radical choice for someone who hadn't been diagnosed with breast cancer yet," Rose, 38, told Fox News Digital.
"But I lost my mom when I was 16. And by the time I was 16, I had lost my grandmother, my great aunt, almost every woman in my family to this disease. And I said that legacy ends with me.

Allyn Rose competed in both the Miss America and Miss USA pageants. She won the Miss Maryland USA title in 2011 and later competed at the national Miss USA pageant that year. (Miss Universe Organization/Courtesy of Allyn Rose)

"I don't want that to be my story," she said. "I don't want to have to tell my 16-year-old daughter someday that she's going to have to spend the rest of her life without her mom. This sad family legacy was not going to take my life if I had anything to do with it."

Rose's mother, Judy Rose, was first diagnosed with breast cancer at 27 and had her right breast removed. The cancer later developed in her remaining breast, reaching Stage 3, according to People magazine. Judy died at 51.
Allyn Rose’s mother, Judy Rose, died from breast cancer in 2004. (Courtesy of Allyn Rose)

Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in the U.S. after skin cancers, accounting for about one in three new cancer cases diagnosed in women each year, according to the American Cancer Society. About one in eight U.S. women will develop breast cancer during their lives.
WATCH: ALLYN ROSE CHOSE DOUBLE MASTECTOMY AT 26, SO CANCER LEGACY 'ENDS WITH ME'
The organization estimates that 321,910 new cases of invasive breast cancer will be diagnosed among U.S. women in 2026 and that about 42,140 women will die from the disease.
FOX NEWS MEDIA TEAMS UP WITH BREAST CANCER RESEARCH FOUNDATION
Allyn Rose's mother Judy with her children (Courtesy of Allyn Rose)

Rose was considered to be at elevated risk of developing breast cancer because of her extensive family history. In 2012, she was crowned Miss District of Columbia, earning the opportunity to represent the district at the 2013 Miss America pageant. That same year, at 24, Rose announced her decision to undergo a preventive double mastectomy. She had the surgery two years later, at 26.
Allyn Rose had a double mastectomy at age 26. (Miss Universe Organization/Courtesy of Allyn Rose)

For women with a strong family history of breast cancer, a bilateral risk-reducing mastectomy can lower the risk of developing the disease by up to 90%, according to the National Cancer Institute. The procedure does not eliminate the risk entirely because it is impossible to remove all breast tissue that could become cancerous.

"So much of my life and my identity was wrapped up in the way that I looked and how I presented myself to the world," Rose said. "I paid my bills and my rent with the way that I looked. I didn't think [my looks] were 100% of my identity, but I would be lying if I didn't consider the repercussions of having a surgery like this.

"It would very likely end my modeling career, my career in pageantry, my career really in the entertainment industry. There were so few women talking about having a procedure like this and coming out on the other side.

Randi Sundquist, Miss Nevada; Allyn Rose, Miss District of Columbia; and Mallory Hytes Hagan, Miss New York, perform during the opening of the 2013 Miss America Pageant at PH Live at Planet Hollywood Resort & Casino in Las Vegas Jan. 12, 2013. (Getty Images)

"I wasn't married," she said. "I didn't have any children. These were all conversations I was going to have with a future partner someday. And, so, it was a really tough choice, and it's one that I'm glad that I made, but it's very difficult to make the decision to have a surgery to prevent a cancer that didn't exist yet."
Allyn Rose after her surgery (Courtesy of Allyn Rose)

With her father's support, Rose underwent a preventive double mastectomy to reduce her risk of developing breast cancer. She ended up having three surgeries, including reconstruction, and went through what she described as "very graphic periods of looking completely different, having no breasts, wondering who is ever going to be happy looking at me like this."
Allyn Rose lost her mother, grandmother and great aunt to breast cancer. (Miss Universe Organization/Courtesy of Allyn Rose)
Then she remembered her mother, Judy.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Allyn Rose with her family. (Courtest of Allyn Rose)

"[Losing my mother] drastically impacted my life, not only because it was my mother, but because I didn't know how to be a woman yet," she said. "[When I lost her] I hadn't even gotten my driver's license. I hadn't graduated from high school. I hadn't sent myself off to college yet.

"I spent a lot of those real pinnacle years of my life without a mentor, without someone to guide me through that. It was a very challenging time really, having to be my own cheerleader, experience all those crowning achievements in my life by myself.
"But I think I've come out stronger on the other side of it."
Allyn Rose attends the Breast Cancer Research Foundation's Hot Pink Party at The Glasshouse in New York City May 13, 2025. (Getty Images)
Rose said she received hate mail over her decision, while her father also faced criticism after people learned he had encouraged his daughter to undergo the double mastectomy.
Miss District of Columbia Allyn Rose is introduced at the 2013 Miss America Pageant Meet and Greet Fashion Show at the Fashion Show mall in Las Vegas Jan. 5, 2013. (FilmMagic)

"To see a young person who walked on the Miss USA stage, who worked full-time as a model, who was really in this beauty industry, choosing to almost end my career to prolong my life seemed like a foreign concept," Rose said.

"And there were a lot of radical responses to my decision. I got hate mail. My father received hate mail. People just couldn't fathom that I would take this preventative step. But I didn't want cancer to be part of my story. I wanted it to end with me."
Miss District of Columbia Allyn Rose speaks at the Date for the Cure to benefit Susan G. Komen For the Cure on Feb. 16, 2013, in Universal City, Calif. (WireImage)
Rose made her decision before actress Angelina Jolie publicly revealed that she had undergone a preventive double mastectomy after genetic testing showed she carried a harmful BRCA1 gene variant.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Angelina Jolie poses ahead of a screening of the film "Coutures" at the Pathe Palace cinema in Paris Feb. 9, 2026. (Thomas Samson/AFP via Getty Images)

In a May 2013 New York Times op-ed, Jolie explained that her mother had battled cancer for nearly a decade before dying at 56. Jolie said her doctors estimated she had an 87% risk of developing breast cancer and a 50% risk of ovarian cancer. She chose to have both breasts removed, which she said reduced her estimated breast cancer risk to less than 5%.
Jolie, who was 37 at the time, said she shared her experience so other women could better understand their own risks and options.

Miss Maryland USA Allyn Rose attends a bike build celebrating the 60th anniversary of the Miss USA Pageant and the 70th anniversary of the USO at Pier 88 May 26, 2011, in New York City. (Getty Images)

Rose said she thought her modeling career was over. But in 2019, Sports Illustrated Swimsuit featured her, making her the first woman who had undergone a double mastectomy to appear in the publication.

Allyn Rose attends the inagural Celebrity Beach Soccer After Party presented by GACP Sports & Sports Illustrated at W South Beach Nov. 17, 2018, in Miami Beach, Fla. (Getty Images for GACP Sports & Sports Illustrated)
Today, Rose travels across the country to raise awareness about "the power in prevention."
Allyn Rose later became the first woman who had undergone a double mastectomy to model for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit. (Courtesy of Allyn Rose)

"The thing I wish someone had told me when I was first navigating this was that there is a light at the end of the tunnel," Rose said. "Everything was a question. It was this fear of the unknown. But I said to myself, 'I'm going to still chase all of those dreams. I'm going to go accomplish all the things that I wanted to.'"
When she looks back on her journey, one person comes to mind: her mother, Judy.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Allyn Rose's late mother Judy   (Courtesy of Allyn Rose)

"I do think about what my mom would think, and I know she would be incredibly proud of me," Rose said, fighting back tears. "One of the last things she said to me was, 'Don't let my life be in vain.' And I made a promise to her that I would make use of every day that she didn't have.
"And, so, that has been my mission from the day that she passed to ensure that I could help as many women as possible not have to walk their lives without their mom. That's my goal.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Allyn Rose attends the Breast Cancer Research Fund Awards Luncheon at New York Hilton Midtown Oct. 16, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images)

"I have two children," Rose said. "They don't have the same gene mutation that I have. They no longer have an increased risk of cancer. And that legacy ended with me, and I know my mom would be very proud that I did that."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Liam Neeson, 74, says he doesn't need a gym to stay ready for action scenes
summary: Liam Neeson reveals he skips the gym entirely at 74, relying on daily walks and a year-round fitness approach to keep doing his own action scenes.
story: Liam Neeson told Fox News Digital how he maintains his fitness at 74 and prepares for physically demanding action roles without regularly going to the gym.
Liam Neeson's action movie shape doesn't require time in the gym.
During an interview with Fox News Digital, the actor, who stars in the newly released movie "The Mongoose," discussed how he stays in such good shape at 74.

"No, I don't go to a gym at all, but it behooves me, any actor or actress playing a lead, it behooves you to have a level of fitness," Neeson said. "You don't have to spend two hours in the gym every day. I used to, many years ago, but I keep reasonably fit."
Liam Neeson revealed he does to maintain his physique for action movies at 74. (Getty Images)

title: Miranda Lambert's friend kidnapped by her own father at age 7 recalls daring rescue that brought her home
summary: Lauren Burns was 7 when her father abducted her from Dallas to Jordan. Miranda Lambert's family helped spark the daring rescue mission home.
story: Lauren Burns reveals how her father kidnapped her and took her to Jordan at age 7 and how Miranda Lambert's family helped her mother fight to bring her home. She has written a memoir, ‘Stolen.’

Lauren Burns was dressed in a cheerleader costume for Halloween weekend in 1987 when she climbed into her father's car. But instead of taking her trick-or-treating, he drove the 7-year-old to the airport and flew her thousands of miles from her Dallas home.

Ali Bayan assured the little girl that the trip to his home country of Jordan was a "surprise" and that her mother, Cathy Mahone, knew all about it. But as days turned into weeks and her father refused to let her speak to her mother, Burns began to realize she might never return home.
"I didn't think I would ever see my mother again," Burns recalled to Fox News Digital.
MIRANDA LAMBERT, CARRIE UNDERWOOD 'SHOULD GET A RIBBON' FOR SURVIVING COUNTRY MUSIC IN MALE-DOMINATED ERA
Miranda Lambert's (left) childhood friend, Lauren Burns (right), has written a memoir about her abduction and miraculous rescue. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

Burns recounts the abduction and the international rescue mission it sparked in her memoir, "Stolen." Her childhood friend, country music superstar Miranda Lambert, whose family played a crucial role in bringing Burns home, wrote the foreword.
Fox News Digital reached out to Lambert for comment.
Miranda Lambert performs onstage during the 61st Academy of Country Music Awards at MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas May 17, 2026. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for ACM)
"By the time I was 6 weeks old, my parents got divorced," Burns said.
WATCH: MIRANDA LAMBERT'S FRIEND RECALLS BEING KIDNAPPED BY FATHER AT AGE 7

"All I ever knew was that kind of upbringing. I went between two homes. My mother had full custody of me when I was 6 weeks old, but she did not want to keep me from my father. He was a good dad. He was loving and kind. I saw him almost every other weekend or maybe extra if she needed help. They had a good relationship despite the reasons that they had gotten divorced."
During the drive to the airport, Burns wondered why her stepmother and siblings weren't coming along.
Cathy Mahone and Ali Bayan during happier times. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

"He'd never done anything to make me feel like I couldn't trust him," Burns said. "He was my dad, my provider. He was the one that loved me dearly. So, if he tells me something, I'm going to trust him. But it didn't quite add up."
Lauren Burns as a baby with her father, Ali Bayan. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

Burns' parents met while Mahone, a Christian, was working as a waitress and Bayan, a Muslim, was studying engineering in Texas. Mahone had full custody, but Bayan, who owned a restaurant in Dallas, saw his daughter regularly. There were "no red flags," Burns said, until that Halloween weekend.

The Monday after Halloween weekend, Mahone went to Burns' elementary school to have lunch with her, as she typically did. She expected to hear about her daughter's weekend of trick-or-treating with her father. Instead, she discovered that Burns had never arrived at school. She soon learned that her ex-husband had abducted their daughter and taken her to Jordan.
Lauren Burns on Halloween with her mother before her abduction. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

A desperate Mahone rushed to a pay phone. She called the one man she believed could help her — Miranda Lambert's father, Rick Lambert. The former Dallas police officer ran a private detective agency with his wife, Beverly.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Rick Lambert is a former Dallas police officer. (Rick Diamond/Getty Images for BMI)

"Rick and Beverly were home," Burns said. "They got Miranda, they moved out of their house and they were with my mom day and night trying to figure out a way to help my mom get me back. They were calling everyone they knew. Rick pulled some strings and got an appointment at the Dallas County Courthouse, so my mom could try to get a warrant out for my father's arrest."
The Lamberts had known Mahone for years, long before Burns and Miranda were born. Their friendship began when Mahone worked for Miranda's grandmother, Wanda, at an apartment complex.
Beverly Lambert and Lauren Burns in 1987. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

Until then, Burns had traveled only to Florida to visit her grandmother. Now, the 7-year-old was in the Middle East, unable to speak Arabic and struggling to adjust to unfamiliar customs and a different way of life.
Lauren Burns with her mother in Florida, circa 1985. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

"I had to cover my hair," Burns said. "I could not wear shorts. We had to take our shoes off and wash our feet. There were no toilets. It was a hole in the ground with a chain above. I had never seen anything like that. Even the way we ate, it was a communal type of eating. You would sit on the floor with a big rug that was underneath and big plates of food, fresh food. You could smell all the different spices and the fresh hummus. We would all sit together, and you would eat with your hands."
But for Burns, the most painful change was in the father she had always trusted. Once in Jordan, the man she viewed as her protector became "distant."
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
"Stolen: A True Story ― Kidnapped, Rescued, Redeemed" by Lauren Burns is available now. (Post Hill Press)

"I quickly realized that my father was not going to take care of me in Jordan like he did in Texas," she said. "It was different roles that I didn't quite understand. I quickly got the sense that it was my grandmother and aunt's job to take care of me because it wasn't the man's job to take care of the child. But at a time in my life when there was so much confusion, I really needed my father. I really needed my mother, and I didn't have that either."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

People stand before the Roman-era South Gate, built in honor of Roman Emperor Hadrian circa A.D. 130, at the Roman ruins of Jerash in northern Jordan on April 29, 2026. Jordan is home to major archaeological sites including Wadi Rum desert, the Dead Sea and Jerash. (AFP via Getty Images)
Back in Texas, Mahone learned that the lack of an extradition treaty with Jordan severely limited the U.S. government's ability to help her.

Determined to get her daughter back, Mahone turned to a North Carolina-based security firm staffed by former special operations personnel. She paid the team $80,000 and sold her jewelry to cover living expenses. There was no guarantee she would see her daughter again.
Two rescue operatives in Jordan, circa 1988. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

The team spent weeks searching for Burns before tracking her to Jerash, Jordan, where Bayan had enrolled her in school. Mahone accompanied the team to Jordan, disguising herself as they prepared to rescue her daughter.
Lauren Burns' escape route (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)
Burns was sitting on a school bus when she spotted her mother.

"My mom had her hair covered," Burns said. "She came over and tapped the window. I looked straight into my mother's eyes, and all I could think of was that it looks just like my mom, but how can it be? I thought I was dreaming. My mom started motioning me to come and get off the bus, but I froze. So, she had to push her way onto the bus."
Cathy Mahone in Jordan (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

As Mahone boarded the bus and grabbed her daughter, a school chaperone jumped on Mahone's back and tried to stop her. Mahone fought back, punching the woman in the nose before rushing Burns off the bus and into a waiting car.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Lauren Burns after her rescue. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)
The rescue team then drove Burns and Mahone toward the Israeli border, crossing the Allenby Bridge into Israel before making their way back to the United States.
"They put me on the floorboard of a car, they covered me up with blankets, and we sped off," Burns said.
Lauren Burns, left, and her mother, Cathy Mahone (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)
Three months after her abduction, Burns finally returned to the United States, where family and friends — including a young Lambert — were waiting to welcome her home.
A young Miranda Lambert huts Lauren Burns after her return to America. (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)
"The first person I saw when I was coming down that runway was Miranda," Burns said, fighting back tears.

"She was probably 4 or 5 years old, a little thing with this blonde hair. She was running and pushing past all the other people. … And when we got home, my aunt had left every single Christmas tree up. She refused to take down the decorations because she said, 'Lauren will come home and we will celebrate Christmas.' So we celebrated Christmas and opened presents that year in January when I returned."
Lauren Burns in 1985 (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

But returning home did not mean the ordeal was over. Fearing Bayan might abduct Burns again, Mahone kept her daughter in hiding, repeatedly moving to protect her. Burns said she had moved 14 times by the time she reached high school, leaving her struggling to find a sense of stability.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Lauren Burns with Miranda Lambert's parents (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)

As a teenager, Burns grew increasingly angry. Beverly urged Mahone to let Burns stay at the Lamberts' farmhouse in Lindale, Texas — the same home Miranda Lambert later sang about in "The House That Built Me" — to help her through a difficult period.

Beverly quickly welcomed Burns into her church community and even "handpicked my friends," as Burns recalled, determined to surround the struggling teenager with positive influences. With the Lamberts by her side, Burns grew stronger in her Christian faith. She "hated Father's Day" for years but always wrote a card to Rick Lambert, who became a father figure in her life.

Bev Lambert, Miranda Lambert and Rick Lambert pose at BMI Honors Miranda Lambert for her first No. 1 single with a 1940s-style bash at The Cellar in Nashville Feb. 26, 2010. (Rick Diamond/Getty Images for BMI)

The bond endured as Burns grew up alongside Lambert, whom she described as "like a little sister to me." Long before Lambert became a country music superstar, Burns knew her as the little girl whose family had welcomed her into their home.
Lauren Burns and Miranda Lambert as children (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)
Bayan was indicted while abroad and arrested in 1990 after returning to the United States, People magazine reported. He was sentenced to eight years probation.
Burns was in high school when she finally confronted him, asking why he had abducted her.
As a teen, Lauren Burns confronted her father. (lauren burns)

"He wanted to raise me in his country, with his family," Burns said. "The only way he could do that was to take me. He wanted me to be raised in his beliefs and his culture. He said, 'I felt like I was doing the best thing for you.'"
Lauren Burns (Courtesy of Lauren Burns)
While Burns forgave Bayan, they have not spoken since 2019, People magazine reported. Fox News Digital could not reach Bayan for comment.

"If my 7-year-old self could look at my life today," Burns said, "she would say, 'There is hope.' There is healing on the other side of forgiveness. There is freedom when you can let go. There is life, abundant life. And there is a way out."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Selma Blair breaks silence, weeks after arrest for alleged assault
summary: Actress Selma Blair broke her silence Friday, weeks after being arrested for an alleged assault on flight attendants on a Delta flight.
story: Blair, walking with her service dog, is doing photo ops for fans at '90s Con in Connecticut. (Obtained by Fox News)
Selma Blair on Friday apologized following her arrest after an alleged altercation with flight attendants on a Delta flight earlier this month.

The 54-year-old actress said her lawyers advised her not to say anything because of the ongoing legal matter but added, "Not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life. And, so, to the people I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed, I am so sorry."
In the emotional Instagram video, taken in what appeared to be her home, she added that she would be taking care of her health and her son "and thinking of you all with gratitude and love."

Blair was arrested for assault and arraigned Oct. 12 on two counts of second-degree assault stemming from alleged attacks on a Port Authority police officer and a nurse following her arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport from Los Angeles. Police had responded to a call about a "physically abusive passenger" aboard Delta Flight 938.
Selma Blair broke her silence on Instagram after her arrest. (Sean Zanni)
SELMA BLAIR'S REP SPEAKS OUT AFTER STAR'S ARREST: ‘MUCH MORE TO THIS STORY’
Blair pleaded not guilty. The judge set bail at $20,000 cash, $60,000 bond or $60,000 partially secured bond. She's expected in court in January 2027.

"On Sunday, October 11, at approximately 11 p.m. at JFK Airport, PAPD responded to a call about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Airlines flight 938, which was parked at the gate after arrival from LAX," New York Port Authority officials confirmed to Fox News Digital.
"Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation."

According to court documents, Blair was restrained on a stretcher at the airport but freed her leg and allegedly kicked an officer in the face, neck and chest, causing substantial swelling. A nurse at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center, where Blair was taken, alleged that the actress kicked her in the chest while moving her.
Selma Blair appears in Queens Criminal Court Oct., 12, 2026 in Queens, N.Y. (Barry Williams/ New York Daily News via Pool)
Delta confirmed that law enforcement officials responded to an incident upon arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport, a flight that departed Los Angeles earlier in the day.

"Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first," Delta said in a statement. Sources told TMZ that Blair punched one flight attendant and bit another in the middle of the flight.
Law enforcement officials confirmed Blair was also separately served with a summons by the FBI and is facing one charge of assault.

At the time, the New York Post reported that Blair's lawyer told the court that the actress "missed several doses of … a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms."
Representatives for Blair later shared a lengthy statement with People, saying the actress "did not intend to harm anyone."
"Since Sunday night, the public account of what happened to Selma aboard a flight to New York has been built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline," the spokesperson said.

"A handful of journalists have taken the time to report on Selma as a human being rather than a headline, and we are grateful to them," the statement continued. "But fair reporting has been the exception, and in the space left by our silence, speculation has hardened into something being treated as fact.

"We can, however, correct the record on a few points already in public circulation. Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight. There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone."

title: John Mellencamp says he’ll ‘probably be totally deaf’ after upcoming tour as hearing problems worsen
summary: John Mellencamp says he'll "probably be totally deaf" by the end of his upcoming tour but refuses hearing aids, citing his grandmother's advice.
story: Teddi Mellencamp told Fox News Digital that her father, John Mellencamp, came to the hospital every day while she was battling stage 4 cancer.
John Mellencamp isn't ready to give up the stage, even if his hearing continues to deteriorate.

The 75-year-old rock icon revealed he could be "totally deaf" by the time his upcoming tour ends, as he opened up about his worsening hearing and tinnitus during an appearance on the "Nepo, Baby!" podcast.
"I don't like going out 'cause I can't hear," Mellencamp said when asked about his hearing difficulties.
JOHN MELLENCAMP SHARES HIS UNCONVENTIONAL ADVICE TO HIS CHILDREN ABOUT WORK
John Mellencamp revealed he could be "totally deaf" by the end of his upcoming tour as he struggles with worsening hearing problems. (Timothy Norris/Getty Images for The Recording Academy)

The "Jack & Diane" singer acknowledged that years of exposure to loud rock music may have taken a toll, explaining that he experiences ringing in his ears and pulsatile tinnitus, a condition that causes him to hear his heartbeat.

"I mean, it's like right now my ears are ringing like crazy, and I have pulsatile tinnitus, which is, I hear my heartbeat. And we go into a restaurant, and it's just like, 'Well, I'm out,' because I can't hear anything because I hear all this noise and stuff. I'm sure people don't want to keep [repeating things] in my face … so just add tinnitus on top of that and it's impossible."
Pulsatile tinnitus is a rare form of tinnitus that causes people to hear sounds, such as whooshing or thumping, in time with their heartbeat, according to the Cleveland Clinic.
JOHN MELLENCAMP RIPS MODERN POLITICIANS FOR LACKING HUMILITY AND RESPECT
Mellencamp, 75, admitted that ringing in his ears and pulsatile tinnitus have made everyday activities increasingly difficult. (Phillip Faraone/Getty Images for The Recording Academy)
Despite his hearing difficulties, Mellencamp said he plans to continue performing.
When asked whether he planned to keep touring, the musician predicted he could lose his hearing entirely by the time the concerts ended.
"Yeah, I probably will be totally deaf by the time the tour is over. Yeah, but you know, I wear earplugs and stuff, but I do not ever, will I ever get hearing aids."

Mellencamp also explained why he had refused to wear hearing aids, recalling advice from his grandmother that has stayed with him.
Mellencamp refuses to wear hearing aids despite his worsening hearing, citing advice his grandmother gave him years ago. (Gary Miller/Getty Images)

"Well, my grandmother told me, she said, 'John, don't ever get hearing aids because once you get them, you can't live without them.' So, she said, 'If you think chasing around a pair of glasses is a drag, wait 'til you start chasing around a pair of glasses and some hearing aids. And where's your wallet? Where's your car keys?'"
